subject: New phylogenetic comparative method for high-dimensional data

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: New phylogenetic comparative method for high-dimensional data
parts:
Colleagues,

 

I wish to alert you to a new paper of interest to morphometricians that wish to investigate macroevolutionary patterns in shape variation, and require phylogenetic comparative methods. The paper is currently in Early View at Methods in Ecology and Evolution (https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/2041-210X.14438).

 

In this paper, Mike Collyer and I describe a new method, E-PGLS: an extended phylogenetic least squares regression approach for the analysis of high-dimensional data. E-PGLS allows one to utilize more than one individual per species directly in the analysis, rather than relying on species means. The method has two primary purposes. First, it allows one to incorporate within-species variation in their phylogenetic comparative analyses of multivariate data. When used in this manner, it is equivalent to other methods for incorporating within-species variation (e.g., Felsenstein 2008).

 

Additionally, E-PGLS allows one to compare within-species trends across species while simultaneously accounting for phylogenetic non-independence. In this capacity, it is useful for determining whether intraspecific patterns, such as sexual dimorphism, allometry, population-level divergence, etc., differ across species, but does so in a phylogenetically-informed context (something inaccessible with current approaches).  

 

Because morphometricians commonly have datasets comprising many individuals per species, and often wish to incorporate them when evaluating their evolutionary hypotheses, we hope that this new procedure assists you all in your analytical endeavors.


Presently the method is implemented in RRPP as `lm.rrpp.ws`. We are finishing the equivalent function for shape-specific data, to be included in geomorph, and will let you all know when it is ready for distribution.  In the meantime, we encourage you to read the paper and learn what E-PGLS provides.

 

Best,


Dean and Mike

 

Dr. Dean C. Adams
